question.text: Securities can be dematerialised only if the issuer company has:

answer.text: Entered into an agreement with the depository to offer demat facility and the ISIN has been activated
Been listed on the stock exchange for at least 1 year
A net worth exceeding Rs. 100 crore
Obtained a special certificate from SEBI for dematerialisation

explanation.text: The Logic: Physical securities can be converted to demat only if the issuer has an agreement with the depository and the ISIN has been activated. The Trap: 'Listed for 1 year' is not a requirement — even newly listed companies can offer demat once they have the depository agreement in place and an activated ISIN. Note: Without an activated ISIN, the depository system cannot recognize or process the security.
